sanskrit: saṃgṛhītajano 'stabdhaḥ prasannavadanaḥ sadā dātā bhṛtyajanāvekṣī na krodhī sumahāmanāḥ
english: He who keeps his people loyal, unhaughty, ever serene of face, generous, watchful over his servants, free from anger, exceedingly great of soul—

sanskrit: yuktadaṇḍo na nirdaṇḍo dharmakāryānuśāsakaḥ cāranetraḥ parāvekṣī dharmārthakuśalaḥ sadā
english: measured in punishment yet not lax in punishment, an enforcer of the duties of dharma, with spies for his eyes, watching his foes, ever skilled in dharma and artha—

sanskrit: rājā guṇaśatākīrṇa eṣṭavyas tādṛśo bhavet yodhāś caiva manuṣyendra sarvair guṇaguṇair vṛtāḥ
english: such a king, endowed with a hundred virtues, is the one to be desired. And his warriors too, O lord of men, should be furnished with every excellence of quality.

sanskrit: anveṣṭavyāḥ supuruṣāḥ sahāyā rājyadhāraṇāḥ na vimānayitavyāś ca rājñā vṛddhim abhīpsatā
english: Good men should be sought out as allies who can uphold the realm, and they must not be slighted by a king who longs for prosperity.

sanskrit: yodhāḥ samaraśauṭīrāḥ kṛtajñāḥ śastrakovidāḥ dharmaśāstrasamāyuktāḥ padātijanasaṃyutāḥ
english: Warriors valiant in battle, grateful, expert in weapons, versed in the codes of dharma, attended by their bands of foot-soldiers,

sanskrit: arthamānavivṛddhāś ca rathacaryāviśāradāḥ iṣvastrakuśalā yasya tasyeyaṃ nṛpater mahī
english: enriched with wealth and honor, skilled in the maneuvering of chariots, adept with arrows and weapons—the king who has such men, his is this earth.

sanskrit: sarvasaṃgrahaṇe yukto nṛpo bhavati yaḥ sadā utthānaśīlo mitrāḍhyaḥ sa rājā rājasattamaḥ
english: The king who is ever intent upon winning over all men, disposed to exertion, and rich in friends—that king is the best of kings.

sanskrit: śakyā aśvasahasreṇa vīrāroheṇa bhārata saṃgṛhītamanuṣyeṇa kṛtsnā jetuṃ vasuṃdharā
english: With a thousand horses mounted by heroes, O Bhārata, and with men won over to his side, the whole earth may be conquered.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evaṃ śunāsamān bhṛtyān svasthāne yo narādhipaḥ niyojayati kṛtyeṣu sa rājyaphalam aśnute
english: Bhīṣma said: The ruler of men who, after the fashion of the dog, appoints servants each to his own proper station in their fitting tasks—he enjoys the fruit of his kingdom.

sanskrit: na śvā svasthānam utkramya pramāṇam abhi satkṛtaḥ āropyaḥ śvā svakāt sthānād utkramyānyat prapadyate
english: A dog should not be raised beyond his proper station and honored above his measure; should the dog be promoted, he overleaps his own place and grasps for another.

sanskrit: svajātikulasaṃpannāḥ sveṣu karmasv avasthitāḥ prakartavyā budhā bhṛtyā nāsthāne prakriyā kṣamā
english: Wise servants, endowed with good birth and lineage and settled in their own tasks, should be promoted; promotion to a station unfit for them is not proper.

sanskrit: anurūpāṇi karmāṇi bhṛtyebhyo yaḥ prayacchati sa bhṛtyaguṇasaṃpannaṃ rājā phalam upāśnute
english: The king who assigns to his servants tasks suited to them enjoys the fruit that springs from servants endowed with merit.

sanskrit: śarabhaḥ śarabhasthāne siṃhaḥ siṃha ivorjitaḥ vyāghro vyāghra iva sthāpyo dvīpī dvīpī yathā tathā
english: The śarabha should be placed in the śarabha's station, the lion in the post fit for a lion in his might, the tiger as a tiger, and the leopard as a leopard.

sanskrit: karmasv ihānurūpeṣu nyasyā bhṛtyā yathāvidhi pratilomaṃ na bhṛtyās te sthāpyāḥ karmaphalaiṣiṇā
english: Servants are to be set, according to rule, in tasks befitting them; they should never be placed against the grain by one who seeks the fruit of their labor.

sanskrit: yaḥ pramāṇam atikramya pratilomaṃ narādhipaḥ bhṛtyān sthāpayate 'buddhir na sa rañjayate prajāḥ
english: The witless ruler of men who, overstepping due measure, places his servants against the grain—he does not win the affection of his subjects.

sanskrit: na bāliśā na ca kṣudrā na cāpratimitendriyāḥ nākulīnā narāḥ pārśve sthāpyā rājñā hitaiṣiṇā
english: Neither the foolish, nor the mean, nor those of unbridled senses, nor men of low birth should be kept at his side by a king who seeks his own welfare.

sanskrit: sādhavaḥ kuśalāḥ śūrā jñānavanto 'nasūyakāḥ akṣudrāḥ śucayo dakṣā narāḥ syuḥ pāripārśvakāḥ
english: Men who are good, capable, brave, learned, free from envy, not mean, pure, and skilled—these should be his attendants.

sanskrit: nyagbhūtās tatparāḥ kṣāntāś caukṣāḥ prakṛtijāḥ śubhāḥ sve sve sthāne 'parikruṣṭās te syū rājño bahiścarāḥ
english: Humble, devoted, patient, pure, well-born by nature, and of good repute—men who are above reproach each in his own station—such should be the king's outer officers.

sanskrit: siṃhasya satataṃ pārśve siṃha eva jano bhavet asiṃhaḥ siṃhasahitaḥ siṃhaval labhate phalam
english: At a lion's side the man should ever be a lion; even one who is no lion, when joined with a lion, gains a lion's reward.

sanskrit: yas tu siṃhaḥ śvabhiḥ kīrṇaḥ siṃhakarmaphale rataḥ na sa siṃhaphalaṃ bhoktuṃ śaktaḥ śvabhir upāsitaḥ
english: But the lion who is surrounded by dogs, though bent on the fruit of a lion's deeds, cannot enjoy a lion's reward when waited upon by dogs.

sanskrit: evam etair manuṣyendra śūraiḥ prājñair bahuśrutaiḥ kulīnaiḥ saha śakyeta kṛtsnāṃ jetuṃ vasuṃdharām
english: Thus, O lord of men, with such men—brave, wise, deeply learned, and well-born—one may conquer the whole earth.

sanskrit: nāvaidyo nānṛjuḥ pārśve nāvidyo nāmahādhanaḥ saṃgrāhyo vasudhāpālair bhṛtyo bhṛtyavatāṃ vara
english: Neither one ignorant of medicine, nor a crooked man, nor an unlearned one, nor one without great wealth should be taken to his side as a servant by guardians of the earth, O best of those who employ servants.

sanskrit: bāṇavad visṛtā yānti svāmikāryaparā janāḥ ye bhṛtyāḥ pārthivahitās teṣāṃ sāntvaṃ prayojayet
english: Like arrows loosed, men intent upon their master's business speed forth; toward those servants who seek the king's good he should employ gentle, conciliating words.

sanskrit: kośaś ca satataṃ rakṣyo yatnam āsthāya rājabhiḥ kośamūlā hi rājānaḥ kośamūlakaro bhava
english: The treasury must always be guarded by kings with diligent effort, for kings are rooted in the treasury; be one who makes the treasury his root.

sanskrit: koṣṭhāgāraṃ ca te nityaṃ sphītaṃ dhānyaiḥ susaṃcitam sadāstu satsu saṃnyastaṃ dhanadhānyaparo bhava
english: Let your granary too be ever full, well stocked with grain, and always entrusted to honest men; be one devoted to wealth and grain.

sanskrit: nityayuktāś ca te bhṛtyā bhavantu raṇakovidāḥ vājināṃ ca prayogeṣu vaiśāradyam iheṣyate
english: Let your servants be ever ready and skilled in battle; and skill in the handling of horses is desired here as well.

sanskrit: jñātibandhujanāvekṣī mitrasaṃbandhisaṃvṛtaḥ paurakāryahitānveṣī bhava kauravanandana
english: Watchful over your kinsmen and relations, surrounded by friends and connections, and seeking the welfare of the townsfolk's affairs—so be, O delight of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: eṣā te naiṣṭhikī buddhiḥ prajñā cābhihitā mayā śvā te nidarśanaṃ tāta kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: This conclusive wisdom and insight I have declared to you; the dog is your illustration, my son. What more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca rājavṛttāny anekāni tvayā proktāni bhārata pūrvaiḥ pūrvaniyuktāni rājadharmārthavedibhiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Many a course of royal conduct you have set forth, O Bhārata—observances ordained of old by the ancients, who knew the dharma and the purposes of kingship.

sanskrit: tad eva vistareṇoktaṃ pūrvair dṛṣṭaṃ satāṃ matam praṇayaṃ rājadharmāṇāṃ prabrūhi bharatarṣabha
english: That very teaching, declared at length, seen by the ancients and held to be the opinion of the good—the essence of the duties of kings—expound to me, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca rakṣaṇaṃ sarvabhūtānām iti kṣatre paraṃ matam tad yathā rakṣaṇaṃ kuryāt tathā śṛṇu mahīpate
english: Bhīṣma said: The protection of all beings—this is held to be the highest duty of the warrior caste. Hear, O lord of earth, how he may render such protection.

sanskrit: yathā barhāṇi citrāṇi bibharti bhujagāśanaḥ tathā bahuvidhaṃ rājā rūpaṃ kurvīta dharmavit
english: As the peacock, devourer of serpents, wears its many-colored plumes, so should the king who knows dharma assume a form of many kinds.

sanskrit: taikṣṇyaṃ jihmatvam ādāntyaṃ satyam ārjavam eva ca madhyasthaḥ sattvam ātiṣṭhaṃs tathā vai sukham ṛcchati
english: Sharpness, crookedness, sternness, truth, and uprightness—holding the mean and abiding in firmness of character, he attains happiness.

sanskrit: yasminn arthe hitaṃ yat syāt tad varṇaṃ rūpam āviśet bahurūpasya rājño hi sūkṣmo 'py artho na sīdati
english: In whatever matter a certain hue would serve his interest, that color and form he should assume; for a king of many forms, even the subtlest aim does not fail.

sanskrit: nityaṃ rakṣitamantraḥ syād yathā mūkaḥ śaracchikhī ślakṣṇākṣaratanuḥ śrīmān bhavec chāstraviśāradaḥ
english: He should ever keep his counsel guarded, mute as the autumn peacock; soft of speech and slender of frame, prosperous, he should be deeply versed in the sciences.

sanskrit: āpaddvāreṣu yattaḥ syāj jalaprasravaṇeṣv iva śailavarṣodakānīva dvijān siddhān samāśrayet
english: At the gateways of calamity let him be watchful, as at the outpourings of water; and as the rain-waters of the mountain seek the heights, so let him resort to the twice-born and the perfected sages.

sanskrit: arthakāmaḥ śikhāṃ rājā kuryād dharmadhvajopamām nityam udyatadaṇḍaḥ syād ācarec cāpramādataḥ loke cāyavyayau dṛṣṭvā vṛkṣād vṛkṣam ivāplavan
english: Desiring his ends, the king should raise his crest like a banner of dharma; ever should he hold the rod of punishment uplifted, and act without negligence—observing income and outlay in the world, as a bird flits from tree to tree.

sanskrit: mṛjāvān syāt svayūthyeṣu bhāvāni caraṇaiḥ kṣipet jātapakṣaḥ parispanded rakṣed vaikalyam ātmanaḥ
english: He should be cleanly among his own flock, and scatter the matters at hand with his feet; once fledged he should stir himself to motion, and guard himself against any weakness.

sanskrit: doṣān vivṛṇuyāc chatroḥ parapakṣān vidhūnayet kānaneṣv iva puṣpāṇi barhīvārthān samācaret
english: He should lay bare the faults of his foe and shake off the enemy's party; like a peacock among the blossoms in the forest, so should he go about gathering his aims.

sanskrit: ucchritān āśrayet sphītān narendrān acalopamān śrayec chāyām avijñātāṃ guptaṃ śaraṇam āśrayet
english: He should take refuge with kings who are exalted, flourishing, and steadfast as mountains; he should seek a shade unperceived and resort to a hidden shelter.

sanskrit: prāvṛṣīvāsitagrīvo majjeta niśi nirjane māyūreṇa guṇenaiva strībhiś cālakṣitaś caret na jahyāc ca tanutrāṇaṃ rakṣed ātmānam ātmanā
english: With neck darkened as in the rains, let him plunge into the night in lonely places; like the peacock by its very nature, let him move unobserved among women. He should never cast off his armor, but guard himself by himself.

sanskrit: cārabhūmiṣv abhigamān pāśāṃś ca parivarjayet pīḍayec cāpi tāṃ bhūmiṃ praṇaśyed gahane punaḥ
english: In the haunts of spies he should shun open approaches and snares; he should harass that ground, then vanish again into the thicket.

sanskrit: hanyāt kruddhān ativiṣān ye jihmagatayo 'hitān nāśrayed bālabarhāṇi sannivāsāni vāsayet
english: He should slay the wrathful, the deeply venomous, the foes who move by crooked ways; he should not resort to immature plumes, but make his dwelling in secure abodes.

sanskrit: sadā barhinibhaḥ kāmaṃ prasaktikṛtam ācaret sarvataś cādadet prajñāṃ pataṃgān gahaneṣv iva evaṃ mayūravad rājā svarāṣṭraṃ paripālayet
english: Ever like the peacock, he should at will pursue what binds him to his purpose, and gather wisdom from every side, as the peacock gathers insects in the thickets. Thus, peacock-like, should the king protect his own realm.

sanskrit: ātmavṛddhikarīṃ nītiṃ vidadhīta vicakṣaṇaḥ ātmasaṃyamanaṃ buddhyā parabuddhyāvatāraṇam buddhyā cātmaguṇaprāptir etac chāstranidarśanam
english: The discerning one should ordain a policy that fosters his own growth: the restraint of self through intellect, the overthrow of others' designs by intellect, and the attainment of self-mastery through intellect—this is the teaching of the scriptures.

sanskrit: paraṃ cāśvāsayet sāmnā svaśaktiṃ copalakṣayet ātmanaḥ parimarśena buddhiṃ buddhyā vicārayet sāntvayogamatiḥ prājñaḥ kāryākāryavicārakaḥ
english: He should reassure his foe with conciliation while marking well his own strength; through self-examination he should weigh his judgment by judgment. The wise man, mind set on conciliatory means, discerns what should and should not be done.

sanskrit: nigūḍhabuddhir dhīraḥ syād vaktavye vakṣyate tathā saṃnikṛṣṭāṃ kathāṃ prājño yadi buddhyā bṛhaspatiḥ svabhāvam eṣyate taptaṃ kṛṣṇāyasam ivodake
english: He should be steadfast, his thought concealed, and speak only when speech is fitting; for the wise man, even were he Bṛhaspati in intellect, who lets out talk too closely held will revert to his true nature, like heated black iron plunged in water.

sanskrit: anuyuñjīta kṛtyāni sarvāṇy eva mahīpatiḥ āgamair upadiṣṭāni svasya caiva parasya ca
english: The lord of earth should inquire into all undertakings, both his own and his rival's, as they are taught in the authoritative scriptures.

sanskrit: kṣudraṃ krūraṃ tathā prājñaṃ śūraṃ cārthaviśāradam svakarmaṇi niyuñjīta ye cānye vacanādhikāḥ
english: The mean man, the cruel, the wise, the brave, and the one skilled in affairs—each he should appoint to his own proper task, along with whatever others excel in counsel.

sanskrit: apy adṛṣṭvā niyuktāni anurūpeṣu karmasu sarvāṃs tān anuvarteta svarāṃs tantrīr ivāyatā
english: Even without himself overseeing those set in their fitting tasks, he should keep them all in tune, as a stretched lute-string holds its notes.

sanskrit: dharmāṇām avirodhena sarveṣāṃ priyam ācaret mamāyam iti rājā yaḥ sa parvata ivācalaḥ
english: Without conflict with any of the duties, he should do what pleases all; the king of whom each man says, 'He is mine,' stands unshaken like a mountain.

sanskrit: vyavasāyaṃ samādhāya sūryo raśmim ivāyatām dharmam evābhirakṣeta kṛtvā tulye priyāpriye
english: Holding firm resolve, as the sun holds forth its far-reaching ray, he should guard dharma alone, making the pleasing and the unpleasing equal in his eyes.

sanskrit: kulaprakṛtideśānāṃ dharmajñān mṛdubhāṣiṇaḥ madhye vayasi nirdoṣān hite yuktāñ jitendriyān
english: Men of good family, nature, and country, knowers of dharma, gentle of speech, in the prime of life, faultless, devoted to his welfare, masters of their senses,

sanskrit: alubdhāñ śikṣitān dāntān dharmeṣu pariniṣṭhitān sthāpayet sarvakāryeṣu rājā dharmārtharakṣiṇaḥ
english: free from greed, well-trained, self-restrained, and firmly grounded in the duties—such men the king, the guardian of dharma and artha, should establish in all affairs.

sanskrit: etenaiva prakāreṇa kṛtyānām āgatiṃ gatim yuktaḥ samanutiṣṭheta tuṣṭaś cārair upaskṛtaḥ
english: In this very manner, attentive and content, aided by his spies, he should watch over the coming and the going of all undertakings.

sanskrit: amoghakrodhaharṣasya svayaṃ kṛtyānvavekṣiṇaḥ ātmapratyayakośasya vasudhaiva vasuṃdharā
english: For the king whose wrath and favor are never spent in vain, who himself oversees his affairs, and whose treasury is founded on his own resolve—the very earth, the bearer of wealth, is his.

sanskrit: vyaktaś cānugraho yasya yathārthaś cāpi nigrahaḥ guptātmā guptarāṣṭraś ca sa rājā rājadharmavit
english: He whose favor is manifest and whose punishment is justly proportioned, who is guarded in himself and whose realm is guarded—that king is one who knows the dharma of kings.

sanskrit: nityaṃ rāṣṭram avekṣeta gobhiḥ sūrya ivotpatan cārāṃś ca nacarān vidyāt tathā buddhyā na saṃjvaret
english: He should ever survey his realm, as the rising sun surveys with its rays; he should know his spies through other spies, and so, by his wit, never be brought to fever.

sanskrit: kālaprāptam upādadyān nārthaṃ rājā prasūcayet ahany ahani saṃduhyān mahīṃ gām iva buddhimān
english: He should take what comes in its due season, and the king should not betray his aim; day after day the wise one should milk the earth as one milks a cow.

sanskrit: yathā krameṇa puṣpebhyaś cinoti madhu ṣaṭpadaḥ tathā dravyam upādāya rājā kurvīta saṃcayam
english: As the bee gathers honey from the flowers little by little, so the king should take his substance and lay up his store.

sanskrit: yad dhi guptāvaśiṣṭaṃ syāt tad dhitaṃ dharmakāmayoḥ saṃcayānuvisargī syād rājā śāstravid ātmavān
english: Whatever remains after the protection of the realm, that serves dharma and pleasure alike; the king, learned in the scriptures and self-possessed, should both accumulate and disburse in turn.

sanskrit: nālpam arthaṃ paribhaven nāvamanyeta śātravān buddhyāvabudhyed ātmānaṃ na cābuddhiṣu viśvaset
english: He should not despise a small gain, nor scorn his enemies; he should understand himself through intellect, and should not place trust in the witless.

sanskrit: dhṛtir dākṣyaṃ saṃyamo buddhir agryā; dhairyaṃ śauryaṃ deśakālo 'pramādaḥ svalpasya vā mahato vāpi vṛddhau; dhanasyaitāny aṣṭa samindhanāni
english: Steadfastness, skill, self-restraint, foremost intellect, fortitude, valor, regard for place and time, and vigilance—these eight are the kindling-fuels for the increase of wealth, be it small or great.

sanskrit: agnistoko vardhate hy ājyasikto; bījaṃ caikaṃ bahusāhasram eti kṣayodayau vipulau saṃniśāmya; tasmād alpaṃ nāvamanyeta vidvān
english: A spark of fire, when sprinkled with ghee, grows great, and a single seed becomes many thousands; marking well these vast workings of decline and increase, let the wise man never scorn the small.

sanskrit: bālo 'bālaḥ sthaviro vā ripur yaḥ; sadā pramattaṃ puruṣaṃ nihanyāt kālenānyas tasya mūlaṃ hareta; kālajñātā pārthivānāṃ variṣṭhaḥ
english: A foe, whether child or grown or aged, will always strike down the heedless man; in due time another would tear away his very root—so the knower of the right moment is the best of kings.

sanskrit: haret kīrtiṃ dharmam asyoparundhyād; arthe dīrghaṃ vīryam asyopahanyāt ripur dveṣṭā durbalo vā balī vā; tasmāc chatrau naiva heḍed yatātmā
english: An enemy would carry off one's fame, obstruct one's dharma, and lastingly cripple one's power in the matter of wealth—whether that foe and hater be weak or strong. Therefore the self-controlled man should never make light of a foe.

sanskrit: kṣayaṃ śatroḥ saṃcayaṃ pālanaṃ cāpy; ubhau cārthau sahitau dharmakāmau ataś cānyan matimān saṃdadhīta; tasmād rājā buddhimantaṃ śrayeta
english: The ruin of the foe, the gathering of wealth and its protection, and the twin ends of dharma and pleasure conjoined—the intelligent man should bring these and yet more to fruition; therefore the king should rely upon the man of intellect.

sanskrit: buddhir dīptā balavantaṃ hinasti; balaṃ buddhyā vardhate pālyamānam śatrur buddhyā sīdate vardhamāno; buddheḥ paścāt karma yat tat praśastam
english: Kindled intellect destroys even the strong; strength, when guarded by intellect, increases; an enemy, though waxing, sinks before intellect—and the deed that follows upon intellect is the deed that is praised.

sanskrit: sarvān kāmān kāmayāno hi dhīraḥ; sattvenālpenāplute hīnadehaḥ yathātmānaṃ prārthayate 'rthamānaiḥ; śreyaḥpātraṃ pūrayate hy analpam
english: The steadfast man who desires all the objects of desire, though his body be slight and clothed in but little vigor, yet as he strives for himself with wealth and honor, fills no small measure as a vessel of his own good.

sanskrit: tasmād rājā pragṛhītaḥ pareṣu; mūlaṃ lakṣmyāḥ sarvato 'bhyādadīta dīrghaṃ kālam api saṃpīḍyamāno; vidyutsaṃpātam iva mānorjitaḥ syāt
english: Therefore the king, even when held in the grip of his foes, should gather the root of fortune from every side; though long oppressed, let him, by the force of his self-regard, be like the sudden flash of the lightning.

sanskrit: vidyā tapo vā vipulaṃ dhanaṃ vā; sarvam etad vyavasāyena śakyam brahma yattaṃ nivasati dehavatsu; tasmād vidyād vyavasāyaṃ prabhūtam
english: Knowledge, or austerity, or abundant wealth—all this can be won by resolute effort; the brahman dwells, intent, within embodied beings; therefore let one know that effort is the source of plenty.

sanskrit: yatrāsate matimanto manasvinaḥ; śakro viṣṇur yatra sarasvatī ca vasanti bhūtāni ca yatra nityaṃ; tasmād vidvān nāvamanyeta deham
english: Where the wise and the high-minded abide, where Śakra, Viṣṇu, and Sarasvatī dwell, and where all beings ever reside—therefore let the learned man not despise the body.

sanskrit: lubdhaṃ hanyāt saṃpradānena nityaṃ; lubdhas tṛptiṃ paravittasya naiti sarvo lubdhaḥ karmaguṇopabhoge; yo 'rthair hīno dharmakāmau jahāti
english: The greedy man one should ever overcome by gifts, for the greedy never reach contentment with another's wealth; every greedy man is grasping in the enjoyment of the fruits of action, and he who is bereft of wealth forsakes both dharma and pleasure.

sanskrit: dhanaṃ bhojyaṃ putradāraṃ samṛddhiṃ; sarvo lubdhaḥ prārthayate pareṣām lubdhe doṣāḥ saṃbhavantīha sarve; tasmād rājā na pragṛhṇīta lubdhān
english: Wealth, food, sons and wife, and prosperity—the greedy man covets all these from others; in the greedy all faults arise here below; therefore the king should not take greedy men into his service.

sanskrit: saṃdarśane satpuruṣaṃ jaghanyam api codayet ārambhān dviṣatāṃ prājñaḥ sarvān arthāṃs tu sūdayet
english: In a meeting he should urge on even the lowliest good man; the wise one should crush all the enterprises and aims of those who hate him.

sanskrit: dharmānviteṣu vijñāto mantrī guptaś ca pāṇḍava āpto rājan kulīnaś ca paryāpto rājyasaṃgrahe
english: A counselor renowned among the righteous, discreet, trustworthy, and well-born, O Pāṇḍava—such a one, O king, is fully fit for the governance of the realm.

sanskrit: vidhipravṛttān naradevadharmān; uktān samāsena nibodha buddhyā imān vidadhyād vyanusṛtya yo vai; rājā mahīṃ pālayituṃ sa śaktaḥ
english: The duties of the god among men, ordained by rule and here told in brief—mark them with your understanding; the king who, following these, ordains them is able to protect the earth.

sanskrit: anītijaṃ yady avidhānajaṃ sukhaṃ; haṭhapraṇītaṃ vividhaṃ pradṛśyate na vidyate tasya gatir mahīpater; na vidyate rāṣṭrajam uttamaṃ sukham
english: If happiness born of misrule, of disorder, and won by violence of many kinds is seen, yet for that lord of earth there is no abiding course, and no supreme happiness arising from his realm.

sanskrit: dhanair viśiṣṭān matiśīlapūjitān; guṇopapannān yudhi dṛṣṭavikramān guṇeṣu dṛṣṭān acirād ihātmavān; sato 'bhisaṃdhāya nihanti śātravān
english: Distinguished by wealth, honored for their wisdom and conduct, endowed with merit, their valor proven in battle, and tried in their virtues—such good men the self-possessed king here soon allies to himself, and so destroys his foes.

sanskrit: paśyed upāyān vividhaiḥ kriyāpathair; na cānupāyena matiṃ niveśayet śriyaṃ viśiṣṭāṃ vipulaṃ yaśo dhanaṃ; na doṣadarśī puruṣaḥ samaśnute
english: He should look to expedients by the various paths of action, and never fix his mind upon what is no true expedient; for the man who sees only flaws attains neither surpassing fortune, nor abundant fame, nor wealth.
